name: Bitter leaf (Vernonia amygdalina)
what_people_do: Wash the leaves to remove bitterness and cook them in soup, or squeeze and drink the bitter juice, for malaria, "sugar" and stomach complaints.
why_they_say_it_works: Bitterness is read as strength; it is said to clean the blood and treat fever.

documented_by.source: Amira OC, Okubadejo NU 2007, BMC Complement Altern Med, PMID 17903257
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Lagos, 225 hypertensive patients: 39.1% used complementary and alternative medicine; among users bitter leaf 9.1%, garlic 69.3%, ginger 23.9%, aloe 4.5%.

evidence.population: Uncontrolled trial, patients aged 12+, Kasese, Uganda
evidence.finding: Adequate clinical response at day 14 in 67% but parasite clearance only 32%; 71% of those recrudesced; no significant toxicity. Uncontrolled, so not good evidence of efficacy.

source.name: Challand S, Willcox M 2009, J Altern Complement Med, PMID 19922255

harm_note: Malaria treated with a leaf instead of an antimalarial is dangerous; the trial does not support that.
gaps: Bitter leaf as soup vegetable not studied.
